summary: This component checks if a blog post is older than one year and displays an appropriate warning notice. If the post has been recently reviewed, it shows a green success message confirming the content is still accurate; otherwise it shows a yellow warning that the information may be outdated. If the post is recent enough, the component returns nothing.

explanations.28: This function returns either a JSX element (the notice to display) or null (nothing to display), depending on whether the post is old.
explanations.29: The useBlogPost hook is a Docusaurus function that gives us access to the current blog post's information, including its metadata.
explanations.30: We're destructuring to get the date and frontMatter fields from the metadata — the date is when the post was published, and frontMatter contains custom fields the blog author added.
explanations.34: useDateTimeFormat is a hook that creates a formatter function for dates; we configure it here once so it can be used in multiple places below. It must be called early because hooks have rules about when they can be called.
explanations.43: The frontMatter object only knows about standard blog fields, so we cast (tell TypeScript) that 'updates' exists and has this specific shape. Without the cast, TypeScript would complain that this field doesn't officially exist.
explanations.49: We spread the updates array into a new array and sort it by date in descending order (newest first), then grab the first element. This finds which update is most recent.
explanations.56: We create a new Date with no arguments, which automatically gives us today's date and time.
explanations.57: We subtract 1 from the current year to get the date from exactly one year ago, which we'll use as our cutoff for whether a post is 'old'.
explanations.59: We compare: if the post's date is earlier than one year ago, then isOld is true.
explanations.67: If a review_date exists and is more recent than one year ago, we consider the post 'recently reviewed' — even if the original post is old, a recent review means the content might still be accurate.
explanations.76: clsx is a utility that lets us combine CSS class names; we're adding both Docusaurus's alert styling and our own custom styles from the CSS module.
explanations.83: The values prop lets us inject dynamic content (the formatted date) into the translated message string, so different languages can have the date in the right place.
